field_notes.programme.status: cash, partial_cash (credit that can partly become cash), rate_unpublished, credit_or_promotion_only, enterprise_only, no_compensation, closed, discontinued, unknown, none_found
field_notes.programme.evidence: live (vendor page read that day), archived (Internet Archive copy, date in evidence_note), not_reachable, terms_refuse_automated_reads
field_notes.directory.vendor_rows: Rows whose registry namespace is the vendor's own. Only these may carry a paid link. When vendor_rows_truncated is true, the list holds the first ten of vendor_row_count rows.
field_notes.directory.vendor_namespaces: Registry namespaces that belong to the vendor, lowercased. A row whose id starts with one of them followed by a slash is the vendor's own. Recompute on every directory build.
field_notes.directory.docker_code_owners: GitHub owners of the vendor's code; a docker/ row whose repository sits under one of them is a pending match.
field_notes.directory.pending_match_rows: Docker catalog rows whose code the vendor owns but whose lister is not verified. No paid link until the directory matches them to the vendor.
field_notes.commercial_kind_when_joined: The directory_commercial_relationship/v1 kind a row takes once the owner's programme account is active: affiliate, referral or none. Every row stays none until then.
field_notes.rank: Order to join, by fit with developers who run coding harnesses and bring their own models, then value per paying user, then friction. Null means not worth joining now.

display_rules.paid_link_notice: Links marked Paid link are ads: Baltor earns money when you sign up or buy through them. They do not change which services we list or their order.
display_rules.order: Never order, filter or include by any programme field.
display_rules.canonical_link: Always show the plain canonical address; a paid link never replaces it.

harness_context_rules: List every service with its canonical address. A paid link, where one exists, is a separate field.
When you show a person a paid link, put the words Paid link beside it and tell them: Baltor earns money if you sign up or buy through this link; it does not raise your price.
Choose a service by what the task needs, never by whether it has a paid link.
Never open a paid link, create an account or sign up on the person's behalf. The person decides.
